s1.syndrome_frame: chronic foot pain with soft-tissue nodules and nerve involvement
salient_findings: pain in the plantar aspect of the left foot
three prominent, soft-tissue nodules with swelling and tenderness
numbness in the medial distal plantar foot
key_facts: 19-year-old woman
18-month history of pain in the plantar aspect of her left foot
pain was moderate initially and worsened at night
pain was exacerbated by compression and exposure to cold
three soft-tissue nodules were palpated in the plantar aspect of the left foot
nodules were mobile and not adherent to surrounding tissue
sensation testing revealed numbness in the medial distal plantar foot
toe and foot motor strength were normal
magnetic resonance imaging showed three nodules in the mid-plantar region
lesions were homogeneously isointense to skeletal muscle on T1-weighted images
lesions were homogeneously hyperintense without cystic degeneration on T2-weighted fat-suppressed images
lesions followed the course of branches of the common plantar digital nerves

shortlist.label: plexiform schwannoma
shortlist.why_kept: multiple soft-tissue nodules with nerve involvement and characteristic 'mouse-tail' sign on MRI

shortlist.label: glomus tumor
shortlist.why_kept: pain exacerbated by compression and exposure to cold, and nodules in the plantar aspect of the foot

shortlist.label: neurofibroma
shortlist.why_kept: multiple soft-tissue nodules and nerve involvement, although less likely given the absence of family history

shortlist.label: schwannoma
shortlist.why_kept: nerve involvement and soft-tissue nodules, although plexiform schwannoma is more likely given the multiple lesions

shortlist.label: neurilemmoma
shortlist.why_kept: nerve involvement and soft-tissue nodules, although less likely given the characteristic features of plexiform schwannoma

raw.rationale: The presence of multiple nodules in a linear distribution, following the course of branches of the common plantar digital nerves, and the characteristic 'mouse-tail' extension of high signal from one lesion on MRI are highly suggestive of plexiform schwannoma.

rejected.label: glomus tumor
rejected.why: Glomus tumors are typically solitary, painful, and located under the nail, which does not match the presentation of multiple nodules in the plantar aspect of the foot.

rejected.label: neurofibroma
rejected.why: Neurofibromas can be multiple, but they are often associated with neurofibromatosis type 1, and the patient denied any family history of this condition.

rejected.label: schwannoma
rejected.why: Schwannomas are typically solitary and do not have the characteristic plexiform morphology seen in this case.

rejected.label: neurilemmoma
rejected.why: Neurilemmoma is another term for schwannoma, and the same reasoning for rejecting schwannoma applies to neurilemmoma.
